classification.difficultyReason: Select useful triangles and intermediate angles without labelled unknowns; the hardest cases require establishing parallelism from equal alternate angles or shared perpendiculars before applying further angle relationships.

content.prompt: In each case, find the size of the marked angle, $\angle AVB$, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle VAB, P on VA and Q on VB; PQ and AB have matching single parallel arrows. Source blue ordinary marks become black.
spec.mathematics: PQ parallel AB; VQP=80 degrees; VAB=75 degrees; marked AVB.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and unknown angle arc only.

answer.worked:
$\angle VBA=80^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $PQ\parallel AB$).
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-75^\circ-80^\circ\\\angle AVB&=25^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle AVB$.

spec.description: Triangle AVB with horizontal VB and PQ; P lies on AV and Q on AB. Matching single parallel arrows.
spec.mathematics: PQ parallel VB; PQA=34 degrees; VAB=60 degrees; marked AVB.

answer.worked:
$\angle VBA=34^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $PQ\parallel VB$).
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-60^\circ-34^\circ\\\angle AVB&=86^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle AVB$.

spec.description: R,V,A collinear; A,P,B collinear; RP crosses VB at Q. Leader arrows identify the narrow angles at R and B.
spec.mathematics: ARP=25 degrees; APR=65 degrees; ABV=27 degrees; marked AVB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angles and required arc.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle RAP$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle RAP&=180^\circ-25^\circ-65^\circ\\\angle RAP&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle VAB=90^\circ$ because $R,V,A$ and $A,P,B$ are collinear. In $\triangle VAB$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-90^\circ-27^\circ\\\angle AVB&=63^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A,P,O collinear and O,Q,B collinear; AQ intersects PB at V. Curved leaders identify A and B givens.
spec.mathematics: OAV=25 degrees; AOB=50 degrees; OBV=22 degrees; marked AVB.

answer.worked:
$\angle APV=50^\circ+22^\circ=72^\circ$ (exterior angle of $\triangle BOP$).
$\angle PAV=25^\circ$ because $A,P,O$ are collinear.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=\angle PAV+\angle APV\\\angle AVB&=25^\circ+72^\circ\\\angle AVB&=97^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle APV$.

spec.description: B,V,P collinear; AV and AP form triangle AVP; BQ parallel AP with matching single arrows. Leader identifies 78 degrees at B.
spec.mathematics: QBV=78 degrees; VAP=28 degrees; marked AVB.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle APV&=180^\circ-78^\circ\\\angle APV&=102^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $AP\parallel QB$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=\angle VAP+\angle APV\\\angle AVB&=28^\circ+102^\circ\\\angle AVB&=130^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle APV$.

spec.description: P,B,A collinear; AV parallel PQ with single arrows; BV joins B to V. Marked angle is the narrow angle at V.
spec.mathematics: BPQ=65 degrees; PBV=135 degrees; marked AVB.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle VAB&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\\angle VAB&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $AV\parallel PQ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=135^\circ-\angle VAB\\\angle AVB&=135^\circ-115^\circ\\\angle AVB&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle at $B$ of $\triangle ABV$.

spec.description: P,V,A collinear and R,Q,B collinear; PQ,QV,VB drawn. No parallel arrows are supplied. All four numerical givens retained.
spec.mathematics: QPV=70 degrees; PVQ=60 degrees; RQP=70 degrees; QBV=70 degrees; marked exterior AVB.
spec.answerVisibility: No inferred parallel marks or answers.

answer.worked:
$\angle QPV=\angle RQP=70^\circ$, so $AP\parallel BR$ (converse of alternate-angle property).
$\angle AVB=\angle QBV=70^\circ$ (alternate angles).

Using the additional given as a check:
$$\begin{align*}\angle PQV&=180^\circ-70^\circ-60^\circ=50^\circ\\\angle VQB&=180^\circ-70^\circ-50^\circ=60^\circ\\\angle QVB&=180^\circ-60^\circ-70^\circ=50^\circ\\\angle AVB&=180^\circ-60^\circ-50^\circ=70^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: P,A,B collinear vertically; PQ horizontal; QV vertical. Right-angle marks at P,Q. AV and BV form a narrow required angle at V; 25 degree leader at B.
spec.mathematics: PQ perpendicular PB and QV; QVA=135 degrees; ABV=25 degrees; marked AVB.
spec.answerVisibility: No inferred parallel marks or calculated angles.

answer.worked:
$PA\parallel QV$ because both are perpendicular to $PQ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle VAP&=180^\circ-135^\circ\\\angle VAP&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $PA\parallel QV$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=\angle VAP-\angle ABV\\\angle AVB&=45^\circ-25^\circ\\\angle AVB&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle at $A$ of $\triangle ABV$.

spec.description: P,A,V,Q collinear; R,B,C,S collinear. Single arrows distinguish PQ parallel RS; double arrows distinguish AB parallel VC. BV joins the two parallel lines.
spec.mathematics: RBA=70 degrees; BVC=40 degrees; marked AVB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given angles and parallel relationships.

answer.worked:
$\angle BCV=70^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel VC$).
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVC&=180^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle AVC&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $PQ\parallel RS$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=\angle AVC-\angle BVC\\\angle AVB&=110^\circ-40^\circ\\\angle AVB&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
